short_bio: Lawyer and founder of the Equal Justice Initiative, author of Just Mercy.
biography:
Bryan Stevenson was born in Milton, Delaware, and studied at Eastern University before earning law and public-policy degrees at Harvard. In 1989 he founded the Equal Justice Initiative in Montgomery, Alabama, to defend people on death row and those sentenced as children.

In 1993 he won the release of Walter McMillian, a man wrongly sentenced to death, the case at the centre of his book Just Mercy (2014); a film adaptation followed in 2019. He argued Miller v. Alabama (2012), in which the Supreme Court barred mandatory life-without-parole sentences for juveniles.

In 2018 his organisation opened the Legacy Museum and the National Memorial for Peace and Justice in Montgomery.
